title: Why retry order is now stable
summary: The queue now advances its cursor only after durable persistence succeeds, preserving retry order when a write fails.

background.text: A queue with two pieces of state
Each worker handles a job payload and a cursor that identifies the next queued item. The ordering guarantee depends on those two pieces of state moving together.

items: The payload records the result of the current job.
The cursor records which job should be processed next.

background.title: The failure window
background.text: If the cursor moves before the payload is durable, a failed write can cause the queue to skip a job.

intuition.text: Treat successful persistence as proof that processing may advance. A failed write leaves the cursor pointing at the same job, so the next attempt observes the original order.

intuition.title: Retry status after a failed write

code.text: The worker keeps the same operations but changes their ordering. An exception from persistence now exits before the cursor assignment is reached.

code.caption: The cursor changes only after persist returns successfully.

code.title: Ordering invariant
code.text: The cursor never identifies the next job until the current job's result is durable.

quiz.question: What directly prevents a failed write from skipping the current job?

options.text: The cursor advances only after durable persistence reports success.
options.feedback: Correct. A persistence failure exits before the cursor assignment.

options.text: The worker sorts each batch before dispatching queued jobs.
options.feedback: The worker consumes queue order and performs no batch sort.

options.text: The client retries each request before checking job status.
options.feedback: Client retry behavior does not govern the server-side cursor.

options.text: The scheduler duplicates each task before assigning a worker.
options.feedback: Duplicating tasks would not make cursor advancement atomic.

quiz.question: What does the queue cursor represent after persistence fails?

options.text: It still identifies the failed job for another processing attempt.
options.feedback: Correct. The failed operation leaves the cursor unchanged.

options.text: It identifies the next job while recovery stores the result.
options.feedback: Advancing early would recreate the failure window this change removes.

options.text: It identifies no job until every worker becomes available.
options.feedback: Worker availability does not determine the cursor value.

options.text: It identifies the first job from the most recent batch.
options.feedback: The queue does not rewind to the beginning of a batch.

quiz.question: Why is successful persistence treated as proof of progress?

options.text: It confirms the current result is durable before ordering advances.
options.feedback: Correct. Durable state makes moving to the next job safe.

options.text: It confirms every worker has completed the current queue batch.
options.feedback: Persistence confirms one result, not a batch-wide worker barrier.

options.text: It confirms the client has stopped retrying the current request.
options.feedback: The server's ordering guarantee is independent of client retries.

options.text: It confirms queued jobs are sorted by their submission time.
options.feedback: Persistence does not sort the queue or establish submission order.

quiz.question: Which execution path leaves the cursor assignment unreachable?

options.text: Persistence raises an exception while storing the current result.
options.feedback: Correct. The exception exits before execution reaches cursor advancement.

options.text: Persistence succeeds while storing the complete current job result.
options.feedback: A successful return permits execution to reach the assignment.

options.text: The cursor references the current job before processing begins.
options.feedback: That is the expected starting state, not an exit path.

options.text: The worker receives another job after processing has completed.
options.feedback: Receiving later work occurs after the relevant assignment.

quiz.question: Which invariant best captures the change's ordering guarantee?

options.text: The current result becomes durable before the cursor moves forward.
options.feedback: Correct. This ordering closes the job-skipping failure window.

options.text: The current cursor moves forward before each worker starts processing.
options.feedback: Moving first could skip work when later persistence fails.

options.text: The current batch completes before any result becomes durable.
options.feedback: Results are persisted per job rather than after an entire batch.

options.text: The current client retries before the scheduler assigns more work.
options.feedback: Client retries and scheduler assignment do not define this invariant.

references.label: Failed writes preserve the current cursor
